references_named: Walter Benjamin, The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction (1935)
Jean Tinguely, Homage to New York (1960)
rationale: The mechanism genuinely enacts the concept: real DOM nodes are removed in a chance-shuffled order, then the script removes every element under body including itself, leaving a truly empty document. The double-coding is precise — Metzger's auto-destruction answered by the web's perfect-copy resurrection, with the surviving trace migrating to the browser chrome (the title tag) rather than the page. The Benjamin framing is earned, not bolted on. Restraint is exemplary: smallest build that completes the thought, dry tone, no wall-text dependency for the surface gag.
reservations: The wit lands slightly less sharply than the best catalogue pieces — the '(deleted — reload to resurrect)' punchline is good but the chance/order staging is somewhat conventional compared to e.g. Random Distribution of π. The Tinguely reference is named but not really enacted in the mechanism.
revision_suggestion: Consider letting the chance-shuffled order itself be the visible argument (e.g. a brief on-page trace of the dissolution path before erasure) so the Tinguely sibling-machine reference earns its place in the mechanism rather than only in the rationale.
